children: SYDNEY--Cochlear said it will defend itself against a shareholder class action related to the profit forecasting that sparked the biggest-ever drop in the hearing-implant maker's stock.
Australia-listed Cochlear on Tuesday said it had received a claim filed against it in Australia's Victoria state. The claim relates to its fiscal 2026 profit forecasting, it said.

In August 2025, Cochlear told investors it expected an underlying net profit for the 12 months through June 2026 of between 435 million and 460 million Australian dollars, equivalent to between US$305.3 million and US$322.9 million.
Eight months later, it slashed its outlook on softer demand in developed markets and uncertainty about Middle East sales, flagging a profit of between A$290 million and A$330 million.
The scale of the downgrade surprised analysts and sparked a 41% one-day drop in the company's share price.
"Cochlear denies the allegations set out in the claim and will be defending the proceedings," Cochlear said.
